summary: Sayori Tsubota is an Indologist who studied as a PhD student at Osaka University (attested 2020). Tsubota held a JSPS postdoctoral fellow position at Tohoku University (attested 2026).
Scarlett J. He works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She was a PhD student at Columbia University (attested 2026), where she also held an academic post.

Schuyler Cammann (1912–1991) worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kent School, Yale, Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and under doctoral supervisor Helmut Hoffmann. He held a long-term post at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1948 to 1982.

Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne. He became a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and president and professor at the Numata Center.
Scott DeLancey (born 1949) is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. He studied under Yungdrung Manang and held a post at the University of Oregon starting around 1982.

Scott Hurley works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied under Elizabeth Harrison and earned his PhD from the University of Arizona in 2001, later becoming an associate professor at Luther College in 2002.

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his doctorate from the Australian National University in 2011, he held posts at Hebrew University, the Australian National University, and the University of Manchester.

Sean D. Gaffney specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, having also studied under Philip Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held a post there.

Sebastian Nehrdich works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from Hamburg and Düsseldorf and studying at Kyoto. He held positions at Hamburg, Düsseldorf, Tohoku University, and UC Berkeley.
Sebastian Pole is a specialist in Indology and other fields. He completed studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.

Sebastião Rodolfo Dalgado (1855–1922) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Pontifical Institute of Saint Apollinaris. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the Curso Superior de Letras (1907) and the University of Lisbon (1917).
See Mui Yian is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi (born 1961) is a historian who earned her doctorate from the University of Cambridge. She has taught at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Jamia Millia Islamia, and Ashoka University.

Seigai Omura (1868–1927) was a scholar of art history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts under Umpei Shinma and Kanō Tomonobu, later serving there as assistant professor and professor.

Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned undergraduate and doctoral degrees from Kyoto University under Kosaku Hamada, serving as a researcher, assistant professor, and professor there.

Seiichi Yagi (born 1932) is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo from circa 1951 to 1955, he held posts at Kanto Gakuin University, Tokyo Institute of Technology, and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) was a legal scholar working in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the First Higher School and University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino, later serving as professor at Tokyo and Aichi Gakuin University.

Seiji Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai (born 1980) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Kyoto University (circa 2005–2008) and became a professor there around 2013.

Seiji Nemoto (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University from circa 1968 to 1972 and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba from circa 2007 to 2014.
